member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Acad.AcadDispatcher
member.summary:
Runs code on AutoCAD's main thread, in the application context, for callers on any thread (the pipe server answers the MCP bridge on thread-pool threads; the AutoCAD API is single-threaded).
Mechanism (AutoCAD 2027, .NET 10). Work items are posted to the WPF of AutoCAD's main thread, captured in (IExtensionApplication.Initialize runs on the main thread). AutoCAD's main window, ribbon and palettes are hosted on that thread, and every Win32 message loop that runs there (the idle main loop, and the nested loops while a command waits for input) dispatches the dispatcher's posted message. An item therefore starts like a palette button click: from the message loop, in the application context, within milliseconds, without the user moving the mouse. While an item runs, is a of the same dispatcher, so every await inside an asynchronous item resumes on the main thread, also while a command is active and waiting for input (which is what typing command input with Document.SendStringToExecute and then awaiting the next prompt needs).
Why not the alternatives. DocumentCollection.ExecuteInApplicationContext is called from a command (on the main thread) to leave the document context, so it does not solve the hop from a background thread. Application.Idle is raised by AutoCAD's idle processing after messages have been handled: a queue drained from Idle needs a wake-up message when AutoCAD is completely idle, and AutoCAD does not document that Idle is raised while a command waits for input, which typing command input step by step depends on. AutoCAD's own Autodesk.AutoCAD.Runtime.SynchronizationContext is installed on the main thread but its scheduling is not documented. The main thread's WPF dispatcher is documented .NET behaviour and is what AutoCAD's WPF palettes and the ribbon run on. still exposes Idle as an "AutoCAD has caught up" signal.
Busy. An item does not start while a modal dialog is open in AutoCAD (AutoCAD's main window is disabled while any modal dialog or message box is shown); it waits for the dialog to close. An item that has not started within fails with . Code already on the main thread runs inline. Once started, synchronous items cannot be interrupted; asynchronous items should honour their cancellation token.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Drafting.DraftingEngine
member.summary:
Types AutoCAD commands and their inputs into the command line VISIBLY, one input at a time, the way a drafter types (the heart of run_commands). Runs on AutoCAD's main thread inside : every await resumes on the main thread in the application context.
Mechanism (chosen for AutoCAD 2027 after comparing the options). Each command and each input is sent with Document.SendStringToExecute(text + "\n", activate: true, wrapUpInactiveDoc: false, echoCommand: true), exactly like keyboard input: AutoCAD echoes it in the command line ("Specify first point: 0,0"), validates it like typed input, and draws the result before the next input is sent. After each input the engine yields to AutoCAD's message loop and polls (30 ms) until AutoCAD has taken the input: a new prompt started (Editor.PromptingForXxx), the command ended/cancelled/failed, AutoCAD became quiescent, or the queued input is gone (Internal.Utils.IsInputPending) and the state changed. Only then, after the watch-mode pause (), is the next input typed. This keeps every input visible and gives the engine a clean point to check the prompt, the command-line messages and the command state between inputs.
Why not Editor.CommandAsync inside DocumentCollection.ExecuteInCommandContextAsync. It passes all arguments of a command in one call like AutoLISP's (command), shows them only through CMDECHO, cannot pause between arguments, cannot see which prompt each argument met or which one AutoCAD rejected, and leaves surplus arguments to the Command prompt. SendStringToExecute is the documented way for modeless UI to type into AutoCAD, and the only one that looks like a person typing.
Safety. The plan was checked by and approved before the engine starts. While typing: an input is never typed when its command has already ended (it would start another command at the Command prompt); an input containing a space or ';' is typed only at a text prompt (elsewhere a space acts like Enter and would split it); TEXTEVAL=0 keeps "(" literal at text prompts; and vetoes any forbidden command AutoCAD is about to run. Dialogs are switched off (); one that still opens is cancelled () and the call stops with its title. The user's Esc stops the call.
Always restored (also on errors, Stop and timeouts): a still-active command is cancelled with Esc, the UNDO Begin/End group is closed, and the system variables are put back.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Plugin.Drafting.SysvarScope
member.summary:
The system variables a run_commands call sets so typed input means exactly what the classic command line means, and always restores. Main thread only.
SYSMON = 0the system-variable monitor prints no "**** System Variable Changed ****" notices into the command line the engine reads (the settings below and the AI's own SETVARs would trigger them).
CMDDIA, FILEDIA, ATTDIA = 0commands prompt on the command line instead of opening dialogs (plot, file names, attribute values).
TEXTED = 1TEXT takes its text on the command line instead of the in-place editor.
TEXTEVAL = 0text answers starting with "(" or "!" are taken literally, never evaluated as AutoLISP.
DYNPICOORDS = 1with Dynamic Input on, "10,0" stays absolute and only "@10,0" is relative.
OSNAPCOORD = 1typed coordinates win over running object snaps.
NOMUTT = 0prompts and messages are shown (the user watches them, the engine reads them).
PICKAUTO = 0a typed point that hits nothing at "Select objects:" selects nothing instead of starting a window.
PICKADD 0 -> 2several picks add up instead of replacing each other.
The original values are also written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\AcadCopilot\drafting-sysvars.json until they are restored, so a crash of AutoCAD in the middle of a call cannot leave the user's registry settings (FILEDIA, CMDDIA...) changed: the next call puts them back first.
